Delta Air Lines and United Airlines also cut their profit outlooks this month. Southwest CEO Bob Jordan said travel demand remains strong despite higher fares. In this article LUV Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Southwest Airlines became the third major U.S. airline this month to cut its 2026 profit forecast due to higher fuel prices, but CEO Bob Jordan said travelers continue to book despite higher fares. The carrier expects to earn between $2.60 and $2.85 a share on an adjusted basis this year, down from its forecast in July of between $3.25 to as much as $4.25 a share. Here's what Southwest reported for third quarter compared with Wall Street expectations, according to consensus estimates from LSEG: Earnings per share: 66 cents adjusted vs. 58 cents expected Revenue: $8.42 billion adjusted vs. $8.25 billion expected Southwest forecast per-share adjusted earnings of between 55 cents and 80 cents in the fourth quarter and unit revenue, a gauge of airfare, up as much as 21% from a year earlier. It said it expects to grow capacity by up to 4% year over year. "Demand remained strong as we lapped last year's bag fee and other commercial initiatives, reinforcing our belief that the earnings power we've built is durable, even with significantly higher fuel costs," Jordan said in an earnings release. The airline said its average passenger fare was $231.69 in the third quarter, up almost 27% from the same quarter of 2025. A spokesman said that number does not include add-on fees. The number of revenue passengers carried fell 3.2% to 33.47 million people. But Jordan told CNBC's Phil LeBeau that demand was strong across every geography and product. "The consumer is incredibly strong and we do not see that abating," Jordan said. "We're seeing strength in both the holiday period and the non-holiday period." Under pressure to grow revenue, Southwest has been remaking its longtime business model over the past several years, scrapping its old policies like two free checked bags per passenger and open seating. In its place, Southwest has started charging for many seat assignments and added a bag fee, similar to major competitors. For the third quarter, Southwest posted net income of $270 million, or 55 cents a share, up from $54 million or 10 cents a share a year earlier. Revenue rose more than 21% to $8.42 billion. Adjusting for one-time items, Southwest reported 66 cents a share. Delta Air Lines and United Airlines also cut their profit outlooks for the rest of the year when they reported third-quarter earnings. Both of those airlines reported top- and bottom-line misses for the third quarter. headlines.article_text: PHP web security flaws spark global alarm: Google, OpenAI, Amazon Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Two critical vulnerabilities, collectively known as “PHP2Shell,” could allow hackers to remotely execute malicious code on affected servers. Governments worldwide have issued urgent security warnings, while Google, OpenAI and other tech companies have worked to identify vulnerabilities and protect affected systems. Amazon detected attempts to exploit the flaws before their public disclosure, but said it remains unclear how attackers obtained information about them. 21 October 2026, Baden-Württemberg, Stuttgart: When visiting the website of the Baden-Württemberg Ministry of the Interior, a warning message appears in the browser indicating a potential security issue. A serious security vulnerability is threatening websites worldwide; blogs, online stores, and news portals could become targets for attackers. The PHP vulnerability allows attackers to take over entire servers. Photo: Bernd Weißbrod/dpa (Photo by Bernd Weißbrod/picture alliance via Getty Images) Picture Alliance | Picture Alliance | Getty Images The tech world is racing to implement fixes after the discovery of critical security vulnerabilities in software used to power much of the internet. The software, known as PHP, is an open-source programming language widely used to power websites and web applications. The discovery of the flaws prompted urgent warnings from governments worldwide, while tech giants including Google, OpenAI and Amazon have been involved in efforts to uncover the vulnerabilities, detect potential attacks and protect affected systems. The two vulnerabilities, collectively known as "PHP2Shell," could allow hackers to remotely execute malicious code on affected servers, potentially exposing sensitive data, according to cybersecurity researchers. While not every website using PHP is necessarily vulnerable, the software's widespread use has raised concerns about the potential scale of attacks. The U.S. National Security Agency on Wednesday urged organizations using PHP to prepare security updates addressing the vulnerabilities, warning that the flaws could provide attackers with direct access to server file systems and databases. The agency recommended taking affected systems offline until the vulnerabilities are fully addressed if immediate updates are not possible. The Federal Bureau of Investigation also warned that malicious actors could exploit the vulnerabilities to execute code remotely, putting sensitive data and networks at risk. Amazon said its threat intelligence team had detected attempts to exploit the vulnerabilities before they were publicly disclosed, using its MadPot threat detection system, which monitors suspicious activity across internet-facing infrastructure. It said the findings suggest malicious actors were already attempting to exploit the vulnerabilities. However, Amazon said it remains unclear how the attackers obtained information about the flaws ahead of their disclosure. Meanwhile, Google and OpenAI highlighted the growing role of artificial intelligence in identifying and addressing cybersecurity threats. Google said its cybersecurity unit Wiz used AI models to help find and investigate the vulnerabilities, while its Gemini AI contributed to efforts to assess the flaws, test potential attacks and verify security patches. OpenAI said researchers working with its AI models had also helped uncover critical vulnerabilities in PHP. The company said it had spent the past two months leading a coalition of software maintainers, cybersecurity researchers and security providers to coordinate fixes and prepare protective measures ahead of public disclosure. The ChatGPT maker described the flaws as among the most significant security issues in recent memory, highlighting both the potential of advanced AI systems to identify vulnerabilities in widely used software and the risk that similar capabilities could be exploited by cybercriminals. Cloudflare, which provides cybersecurity and website infrastructure services, said it had deployed protections against the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities through its web application firewall. The company said its measures were designed to help block malicious requests targeting affected systems, providing an additional layer of defense as organizations work to install software updates. The PHP development team has released security fixes, with authorities urging website operators to identify affected versions and apply the updates as quickly as possible. headlines.title: Comcast beats earnings expectations as media revenue offsets weakness in connectivity
headlines.summary: Comcast is in the process of spinning off its media business into a separate publicly traded company.
headlines.article_text: Comcast (CMCSA) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Comcast topped analyst earnings expectations for the third quarter. Streaming service Peacock hit profitability for the second consecutive quarter. Comcast is in the process of spinning off its media business into a separate publicly traded company. Theme parks and the connectivity business continued to face pressure. In this article CMCSA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The Comcast corporate logo sits at the top of 30 Rock in Rockefeller Center, on August 19, 2026, in New York City. Gary Hershorn | Corbis News | Getty Images Comcast beat Wall Street's expectations for third-quarter earnings — despite headwinds in its theme parks business — thanks to continued strength in its media unit. The company's Peacock streaming service reported a quarterly profit for the second time since its launch in 2020, posting $261 million in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization on $1.8 billion in revenue. Peacock paid subscribers grew to 48 million, up 17% year over year. The streaming platform continued to reap the benefits of record-high viewership for the FIFA World Cup, as the final games played out at the beginning of the quarter and aired on NBCUniversal's Telemundo and on Peacock. Revenue in Comcast's media division, which includes the streaming service, rose 13% compared with the third quarter last year to $5.4 billion. The overall content and experiences unit, which also includes its film studio and theme parks, saw revenue rise 6.5%. Comcast's connectivity and platforms sector, however, continued to face pressure, with revenue down 2.7% year over year. The company reported a net loss in domestic broadband residential customers of 144,000 and a net loss in its cable customers of 274,000 during the period. Its mobile business added 368,000 customers. After years of stagnating growth in broadband and heightened competition from wireless providers like Verizon and T-Mobile, Comcast announced in January 2025 that it would refocus on its mobile business and pursue more competitive pricing plans. Here's how Comcast performed for the period ended Sept. 30 compared with what analysts expected, according to LSEG: Earnings per share: $1.07 adjusted vs. 98 cents expected Revenue: $29.3 billion vs. $29.28 billion expected In June, Comcast announced plans to spin off NBCUniversal and European media business Sky from its core cable, wireless and business services units. The split, which Comcast said would take about a year, will create two separate publicly traded companies. Co-CEO and Chair Brian Roberts said on a call with investors directly following the June announcement that the separation would allow each business to have more "dedicated focus, strategic flexibility, and tailored investment priorities." The decision comes after Comcast spun off most of its cable networks , along with an array of digital businesses, into Versant . That separation was completed in January. For the third quarter, Comcast's revenue was 6% lower than the year-ago period. However, adjusting for the impact of the Versant spin, revenue was essentially flat year over year, Comcast said. Net income for the period was $3.45 billion, or 97 cents per share, compared with $3.33 billion, or 90 cents per share, in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusting for one-time items, including investments and the value of certain intangible assets, Comcast reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.07. The company's theme park revenue fell 4.4% during the period to $2.6 billion, which the company attributed to "cyclical headwinds" and lower revenue from admissions, dented by promotional activity. Adjusted EBITDA for the division sank 17%. The weakness in theme parks comes despite continued investment in the sector with the opening of a new coaster at Universal Studios Hollywood this quarter and Universal's largest theme park property, Epic Universe, last year. Theme park rival Disney reported record quarterly revenue in its park division in August. Comcast's studios division reported revenue of $2.97 billion, down 1.1% from the third quarter last year. Adjusted EBITDA for the segment, however, increased 18.6% to $402 million, thanks to lower operating expenses. The July theatrical release of "The Odyssey," which became Universal's highest-grossing film of all time, boosted the division. Meanwhile, content licensing revenue was down 23.7% from the comparable quarter, leading to the decrease in studio revenue, according to Comcast. Shares of the company rose more than 2% in premarket trading. Here's what the company reported compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $2.00 adjusted vs. $1.88 expected Revenue: $23.3 billion vs. $22.8 billion expected P&G reported fiscal first-quarter net income attributable to the company of $4.73 billion, or $1.97 per share, down from $4.75 billion, or $1.95 per share, a year earlier. Excluding restructuring costs and other items, the company earned $2 per share. Net sales rose 4% to $23.3 billion. Bottles of Dawn dish spray are displayed for sale at a Target store on August 4, 2026 in Washington, DC. Kevin Carter | Getty Images P&G reported volume growth of 2.4%, a strong start for its new fiscal year. Like many consumer companies, P&G has seen demand for its products weaken as shoppers have become more value conscious. Executives have previously said that consumers are now using every last drop of shampoo or laundry detergent, and value packs have become more popular. In fiscal 2026, P&G reported just one quarter of volume growth. P&G is still seeing signs of a bifurcated economy, CFO Andre Schulten said on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Thursday. High-income consumers are willing to trade up to new products, even a $30 shampoo, while low-income consumers are trying to make brands like Tide and Pampers work for their tight budgets. The company has tried to address both ends of the spectrum with promotional pricing, new pack sizes and product innovation that can command higher prices. P&G's top performing division was fabric and home care, which includes brands like Tide and Febreze. The segment's volume rose 4.3% in the quarter. The company's baby, feminine and family care segment and its beauty business both reported volume growth of more than 2%. P&G's grooming division saw volume shrink 0.4% in the quarter. The segment includes Gillette and Venus razors. The company's health care business was the laggard of the portfolio this quarter. Its volume fell 2.9% as demand for oral health care products, like Crest toothpaste, and personal health care items, like Pepto-Bismol, shrank. The company is expecting continued "geopolitical and economic challenges," but P&G is on track to meet its guidance, CEO Shailesh Jejurikar said in a statement. For fiscal 2027, P&G reiterated its forecast for core earnings per share in a range of $6.89 to $7.11. The company is now projecting all-in sales growth in the range of 2% to 4% compared with the prior year, up from its prior outlook of 1% to 3%. The change reflects its acquisition of supplements brand Thorne , which closed on Oct. 1. The launch adds Airbnb rentals to Amex's hotel portfolio, which includes more than 3,400 properties across its Fine Hotels + Resorts and The Hotel Collection programs. Membership points vary by card: Consumer and Business Platinum Card members earn five times the membership rewards on prepaid Airbnb bookings through Amex Travel. Consumer Classic Green Card members earn three times the points on travel bookings made directly through third-party sites, including Airbnb. Other eligible rewards members earn two times the points on prepaid Airbnb bookings through Amex Travel. The changes come as competition among premium credit cards continues to ramp up. Last year, American Express raised the annual fee on its premium Platinum card to $895. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves premarket: TSLA, META, AVEX, SPOT Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Check out the companies making the biggest moves premarket: Aevex — The defense company rose more than 11% after it disputed a Bloomberg News report that said the U.S. Navy would no longer buy Aevex's GARC boat drone due to performance issues. In a release, Aevex said " no orders have been halted ." Lockheed Martin — Shares rose 3% after the defense giant reported better-than-expected results for the third quarter. Lockheed also hiked its earnings and revenue guidance for 2026. Spotify — The audio streaming service gained 5% on fourth-quarter revenue guidance that exceeded analyst expectations. Spotify also said monthly active users rose 11% to 788 million year over year . Energy stocks — The group rose broadly as oil prices surged on renewed geopolitical fears . Kinder Morgan climbed nearly 2%, while APA , Valero Energy and ConocoPhillips advanced more than 1% each. Tesla — Elon Musk's auto manufacturer shed earlier gains and last traded down 3%. Tesla posted beats on the top and bottom lines in the third quarter . The company earned 48 cents per share on an adjusted basis and posted revenue of $28.05 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for 43 cents a share and $27.88 billion. International Business Machines — Shares slipped 5%. The company reported adjusted earnings of $2.95 per share for the third quarter, compared to analysts polled by LSEG's expectations for $2.86 per share. Revenue also beat estimates, and IBM now expects free cash flow for full-year 2026 to increase by more than $1 billion over the year prior. Rollins — The pest control company saw shares fall more than 5% after third-quarter results missed the Street's estimates. Rollins earned 33 cents a share on $1.09 billion in revenue, while the FactSet consensus sought 34 cents a share and $1.11 billion. Meta Platforms — The social media giant slipped 2% even after revenue came in ahead of analysts' estimates. Third-quarter revenue of $64.60 billion topped the LSEG consensus call for $63.37 billion. The midpoint of its fourth-quarter sales guidance was also above the Street's estimates. CSX — The railway company gained 2% after third-quarter earnings beat expectations. CSX earned 57 cents per share on revenue of $4.02 billion, while analysts surveyed by LSEG called for 53 cents a share and $3.96 billion. Revenue per unit increased 7% in the period, compared to the StreetAccount consensus expectation for 5.9% growth. Las Vegas Sands – Shares of the resort company fell 2% after the company posted disappointing third-quarter results. Las Vegas Sands posted adjusted earnings of 54 cents per share on revenue of $3.22 billion. Analysts surveyed by LSEG were expecting 69 cents in earnings per share and $3.35 billion in revenue. Lam Research — The semiconductor manufacturing equipment company dropped more than 7%. Lam sees second-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.33 per share, plus or minus 15 cents, on revenue of $8.60 billion, plus or minus $400 million. That compares to analysts' expectation for $2.31 per share and revenue of $8.53 billion. QuantumScape – Shares of the company behind lithium-metal battery tech surged 7%. QuantumScape announced plans for a 100 megawatt-hour solid-state battery production line for artificial intelligence data centers. Molina Healthcare – The managed healthcare services provider dipped 3%. While third-quarter results beat expectations, premium revenue guidance for the full year is unchanged at roughly $42 billion. The company's guidance metrics across all segments are also reaffirmed. Molina president and CEO Joseph Zubretsky said, "With the apparent plateauing of medical cost trend, which remains at elevated levels, and the strength of recent rate updates for 2027, we believe we are likely observing the beginning of the turn in Medicaid margins." — CNBC's Davis Giangiulio, Sean Conlon, Sarah Min and Paulina Likos contributed reporting.
